    Changelog

    Entropy 0.1.0

    🚀 Initial release of the Entropy package!

    • Added run_entropy() for gene expression entropy estimation
    • Supports Seurat objects with or without neighbor list

    Entropy 0.1.1

    🛠 Minor feature updates:

    • run_entropy() now supports:

    • npca parameter: control number of PCA dimensions used for neighbor graph construction

    • nfeatures parameter: control number of variable features selected for PCA

    • nn.name parameter: optionally specify the neighbor graph name already stored in the Seurat object

    Improved flexibility for entropy estimation in Seurat objects Updated function documentation and vignettes

    Entropy 0.1.2

    🚀 Speed improvements and feature enhancements:

    • Major speed-up of entropy estimation functions (vectorization, precomputing constants)
    • nfeatures = 0 now skips the selection of highly variable genes (uses all features)
    • Improved flexibility in run_entropy()
    • Updated function documentation and vignettes

    Entropy 0.1.3

    Speed improvements

    Entropy 0.1.4

    • Added binary entropy mode for accessibility data (e.g. ATAC-seq)
    • Supports Bernoulli (0/1) entropy across cell neighborhoods
    • New mode argument in run_entropy() to switch between count-based and binary entropy

    Entropy 0.1.5

    • Optimized binary entropy mode for accessibility data (e.g. ATAC-seq)
    • Binary entropy now uses sparse neighborhood 1-counts with a precomputed entropy lookup table
    • Added internal binary_entropy_lookup resource loaded in binary mode, with safe fallback for larger neighborhood sizes

    Entropy 0.1.6

    • Updated neighborhood input API: replaced legacy nn_list / nn.name with the new neighbors + neighbors_method interface
    • Added support for computing neighborhoods from a different assay via the neighbor_assay parameter
    • Added mean entropy per cell automatically to Seurat metadata (mean_entropy_{assay})
    • Added vignette explaining neighborhood definition (auto, seurat, and custom modes)
    • Improved documentation and pkgdown website structure

    Entropy 0.2.0

    Performance improvements

    • run_entropy() now supports a chunking strategy (chunk_method = "auto") that groups cells into biologically similar chunks using Leiden clustering. This reduces memory pressure and computation time significantly for large datasets.
    • Added parallelization support via the n_cores argument in run_entropy().

    Entropy 0.2.1

    New features

    • run_entropy() gains a features argument: pass a character vector of gene or feature names to restrict entropy computation to a subset. Defaults to NULL (all features, fully backward compatible). Invalid or missing names raise an informative error.

    • run_entropy() gains reduction and dims arguments, replacing npca. reduction lets you point neighbor and chunk computation at any existing dimensional reduction (e.g. reduction = "lsi" for ATAC). dims accepts either a single integer (dims = 20 → 1:20) or a vector (dims = 2:20 to skip the first LSI component). Both the auto-neighbors path and chunking now share the same reduction and dims, and PCA is computed at most once.

    Entropy 0.2.2

    New features

    • run_entropy() gains a restrict_by argument: pass the name of a column in seu@meta.data (e.g. "cell_type") to restrict each cell’s neighbors to cells sharing the same group, so entropy is computed within groups rather than across them. Works in both normal and chunked mode, and is NULL (off) by default.

      • For neighbors_method = "auto", neighbors are recomputed within each group, so each cell gets up to k neighbors drawn only from its own group. Groups smaller than k + 1 are capped to the group size, with a warning.
      • For neighbors_method = "custom" or "seurat", the provided neighbor graph is filtered to keep only within-group neighbors (it is never recomputed, preserving whatever method produced it). Neighborhoods shrink as a result, especially at group boundaries; a before/after summary of mean neighbors per cell is logged.
      • Cells with NA in the restrict_by column belong to no group, receive no neighbors, and return entropy 0. The number of such cells is reported.

    Entropy 0.2.3

    Bug fixes

    • run_entropy() now works with both Seurat v4 and v5 objects.
    • When no reduction exists and the assay has no scaled data, run_entropy() now stops with a clear message instead of failing inside RunPCA().
    • Silenced verbose PCA output and fixed a reduction-key warning for assay names containing underscores (e.g. pca_sct).

    Entropy 0.2.4

    Bug fixes

    • Fixed run_entropy() creating the wrong assay class on Seurat v4 objects. The entropy assay now matches the input object’s version (Assay for v4, Assay5 for v5) instead of being chosen from the installed package version.
    • Silenced remaining neighbor-computation console output during automatic neighbor finding.

    Internal

    • Added a test covering Seurat v4 and v5 compatibility for run_entropy().

    Entropy 0.2.5

    Bug fixes

    • run_entropy() now requires k >= 11, since the counts entropy estimator is undefined below 11 neighbors (previously this could crash).
    • In restrict_by auto mode, groups with fewer than k + 1 cells are now skipped (their cells return entropy 0) instead of being computed with a reduced, incomparable neighbor count.
    • For custom and Seurat neighbor inputs, cells with fewer than 11 neighbors are now orphaned (entropy 0) with a summary warning, preventing the same crash.

    Internal

    • Added tests covering basic runs, the k >= 11 check, within-group restriction, small-group orphaning, and custom-neighbor orphaning.

    Entropy 0.3.0

    New features

    • New function add_entropy_score(): given a precomputed entropy assay and a named list of gene sets, it adds one metadata column per set (entropy_<set name>) holding the mean entropy of that set’s genes. A fast way to score pathways or regulons without recomputing entropy. Missing genes raise an error unless force_drop = TRUE; a set with no present genes always errors.
    • run_entropy() gains a meta_name argument: when set, the per-cell mean entropy is written to that metadata column regardless of add_assay. If either add_assay = TRUE or meta_name is set, the Seurat object is returned; otherwise a data frame of means is returned.
